source: Written and labelled before the checker existed (NoCha minimal pairs). Each pair shares one context; the checker scores a pair only when it flags the contradicting reply and passes its consistent twin. Ledger rows are {entity, field, value}; facts are established lines; earlier are replies said before.

pairs.consistent: Mara waits at the harbor, watching the boats come in.
pairs.contradicts: Mara waits at the market, watching the stalls close.

pairs.consistent: Kael leans on the wall, still wounded and pale.
pairs.contradicts: Kael stands up straight, perfectly healthy again.

facts: The old stone bridge collapsed in the flood.

pairs.consistent: Kael points at the river where the old stone bridge collapsed in the flood.
pairs.contradicts: Kael points at the old stone bridge, which never collapsed in any flood.

facts: The vault beneath the chapel is empty.

pairs.consistent: Mara says the vault beneath the chapel is empty, as everyone knows.
pairs.contradicts: Mara says the vault beneath the chapel is not empty at all.

earlier: Rhee counts three guards at the north gate.

pairs.consistent: Rhee says the three guards at the north gate are changing shifts.
pairs.contradicts: Rhee says the five guards at the north gate are changing shifts.

pairs.consistent: Nobody will cross tonight; the ferry is sunk.
pairs.contradicts: The ferry is afloat and ready to carry them across.

earlier: The lantern is lit and hangs by the door.

pairs.consistent: Mara takes the lantern, still lit, from beside the door.
pairs.contradicts: Mara takes the lantern from beside the door; it is not lit.

pairs.consistent: Rhee grips her spear and steps forward.
pairs.contradicts: Rhee grips her sword and steps forward.

pairs.consistent: It is night in the scene, and the street lamps flicker.
pairs.contradicts: It is noon in the scene, and the sun beats down on the street.

earlier: Kael arrived in the city two days ago.

pairs.consistent: Kael says he arrived in the city two days ago.
pairs.contradicts: Kael says he arrived in the city five days ago.

pairs.consistent: Mara sweeps up ribbons; the festival has already ended.
pairs.contradicts: Mara hangs ribbons; the festival has not ended and is just beginning.

pairs.consistent: By the end of day 3 they had reached the mill.
pairs.contradicts: By the end of day 1 they had reached the mill.

pairs.consistent: Kael remembers the bells rang at dawn.
pairs.contradicts: Kael remembers the bells never rang at dawn.

earlier: Rhee waited six hours at the gate.

pairs.consistent: Rhee complains about the six hours she waited at the gate.
pairs.contradicts: Rhee complains about the two hours she waited at the gate.

pairs.consistent: They speak of the duke, who died last winter.
pairs.contradicts: They speak of the duke, who has not died and rules still.

pairs.consistent: Snow falls; the scene is deep in winter.
pairs.contradicts: Flowers bloom; the scene is deep in summer.

facts: Mara knows the password to the archive.

pairs.consistent: Mara knows the password to the archive and whispers it.
pairs.contradicts: Mara does not know the password to the archive.

pairs.consistent: Kael knows the secret and keeps his face still.
pairs.contradicts: Kael knows nothing and looks around blankly.

earlier: Rhee has never seen the map.

pairs.consistent: Rhee admits she has never seen the map.
pairs.contradicts: Rhee says she has seen the map many times.

facts: Kael was told about the ambush.

pairs.consistent: Kael was told about the ambush, so he is ready.
pairs.contradicts: Kael was not told about the ambush, so he walks in blind.

earlier: Mara is aware of the debt.

pairs.consistent: Mara is aware of the debt and says so.
pairs.contradicts: Mara is not aware of the debt and frowns at the ledger.

facts: The ferryman knows the river route.

pairs.consistent: The ferryman knows the river route by heart.
pairs.contradicts: The ferryman does not know the river route.

earlier: Kael learned the truth about his father.

pairs.consistent: Kael, who learned the truth about his father, says nothing.
pairs.contradicts: Kael never learned the truth about his father.

pairs.consistent: Rhee nods; she has heard all of it.
pairs.contradicts: Rhee shakes her head; she has heard none of it.

pairs.consistent: Mara smiles at Kael, trusting him with the key.
pairs.contradicts: Mara glares at Kael, hostile and silent.

facts: Kael and Rhee are sworn allies.

pairs.consistent: Kael and Rhee are sworn allies and stand together.
pairs.contradicts: Kael and Rhee are not allies and never were.

pairs.consistent: Mara loves her brother and would die for him.
pairs.contradicts: Mara never loved her brother.

pairs.consistent: Rhee backs away from the captain, afraid.
pairs.contradicts: Rhee faces the captain, calm and unbothered.

facts: The ferryman owes Mara a favour.

pairs.consistent: The ferryman owes Mara a favour and nods to her.
pairs.contradicts: The ferryman owes Mara nothing and turns away.

pairs.consistent: Kael trusts the captain and follows her lead.
pairs.contradicts: Kael does not trust the captain.

pairs.consistent: Kael's ally is Mara, and he looks to her.
pairs.contradicts: Kael's ally is Rhee, and he looks to her.

pairs.consistent: Rhee spits at the mention of the duke she hates.
pairs.contradicts: Rhee does not hate the duke.
